findings.title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-align-items in align-items mixin
findings.body: The generated rule `-webkit-align-items: $alignment;` is not a valid CSS property and will be silently ignored by browsers. WebKit/Blink supports the unprefixed `align-items` property directly since Chrome 21 (no transitional `-webkit-align-items` was ever shipped). The 2009 flexbox variant `-webkit-box-align` is already included on the preceding line, so this line is redundant noise that bloats the output and signals the author misunderstood the prefix matrix.

findings.title: Invalid CSS property -ms-align-items in align-items mixin
findings.body: The generated rule `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` is not a valid CSS property. The correct IE10 flexbox prefix is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the line above. `-ms-align-items` will be silently ignored by IE10 and IE11, providing no cross-browser benefit while bloating the compiled CSS. This is almost certainly a typo of `-ms-flex-align`.

findings.title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-order in order mixin
findings.body: The generated rule `-webkit-order: $val;` is not a valid CSS property. WebKit/Blink has supported the unprefixed `order` property since the 2012 flexbox spec shipped in Chrome 21; no `-webkit-order` transitional prefix was ever used in production browsers. The 2009-spec prefix `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is already emitted above. This line is dead weight that ignores the actual prefix set and suggests the author did not verify the prefixed property names.

findings.title: order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper has no effect — parent is not a flex container
findings.body: `@include order(2)` is applied to `.extra-info-wrapper`, but its parent `#topic-title` (defined earlier in the same file) is not a flex container: `.title-wrapper` still uses `float: left; width: 90%;` and there is no `display: flex` (or `@include flexbox()`) on `#topic-title` or any of its ancestors in this stylesheet. The CSS `order` property only takes effect on flex items, so this call is effectively dead code and the intended reordering will not happen. Either the parent selector must be promoted to a flex container (and `.title-wrapper`'s float/width reverted) or the `order(2)` call should be removed.
